proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) and a successful published derivation satisfying the two hypotheses of the theorem.  Apply \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\) to its finite derivation DAG.  At initialization, every context \(s\) used by the derivation lies in \(H\), and its normalized kernel is
\[
q_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{p_H(S=s)},
\qquad
p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s)>0.
\tag{7}
\]
The strict inequality follows from \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\) because the sum is nonempty under exact selector support.

The trace invariant gives, after every scheduled node, equality between the emitted labelled kernel after gate reinsertion and the corresponding published kernel.  Concretely, selector correction evaluates the same known zero--one multiplexer; reachable fixing uses
\[
K'_{s,D}=\frac{K_{s,D}}{\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}};
\tag{8}
\]
removal of nonancestors uses \(\sum_Z\prod_{k\in L}K_k\); and a proper-district step uses the same fixed topological quotient.  Each equality is an exact polynomial identity after cross-multiplication.  The regenerated agenda is the unexecuted suffix, so \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\) ensures that the deterministic schedule executes the complete trace rather than stopping or selecting an ineligible token.

Let \(F_H\) be the composite terminal circuit and let \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) be the reduced registry accumulated along this trace.  Every denominator is the supported context normalizer in (7), a reachable fixing margin as in (8), or a reduced elimination denominator with the exact ledger factorization required by \(\textnormal{def:circuit-domain}\).  Hence \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) yields
\[
O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{9}
\]
The terminal published expression identifies the target by the premise of the theorem.  The trace invariant makes its value equal to \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}\), and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) identifies normalized and gate-reinserted target evaluations.  Therefore
\[
F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
\qquad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{10}
\]
No step used a selector value outside \(H\), and (7)--(9) record every division and its positivity premise.  This proves the claimed preservation.

Because \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact selector support gives
\[
p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1.
\tag{11}
\]
Every selector gate is laid back at this value, so its known multiplexer selects the natural response table.  Since \(S\) shares no latent root with \(V\), suppressing its deterministic coordinate removes neither a substantive latent parent nor any root-independence restriction.  Support-active normalization retains every natural response coordinate and substantive latent-root law.  Thus \(G_H^N\), after suppressing \(S\), is exactly the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\).

For every substantive cell \(v\), (11) implies
\[
p_\theta(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})=p_\theta(V=v).
\tag{12}
\]
The intervention \(S=s_{\emptyset}\) changes no laid-back gate, so \(T_{a,H}\) is the ordinary \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\) target.  Applying \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) to (12) proves equality of \(\Phi_H\) and the ordinary observational--target relation.

There is no active selector occurrence, hence \(\Sigma=\varnothing\).  The splitter in \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\) now has exactly the ordinary recursive ID cases: removal of nonancestors, proper-district splitting, and reachable fixing.  Its reachability test is
\[
\operatorname{dis}_{D}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_{D}(W)=\{W\},
\tag{13}
\]
and the successor kernel is \(K_D/\sum_{x_W}K_D\).  The elimination cases are the ordinary finite marginal and topologically ordered district factorization.  Therefore every nonresidual transition agrees algebraically with the corresponding ID step.

At an ordinary residual, \(\textnormal{lem:ordinary-id-residual-compiler}\) completes the comparison.  A successful ID recursion is compiled to a verifier-accepted projection circuit.  A failed recursion returns a hedge and is compiled to a rational support-exact global-twin box with equal strictly positive observational laws and unequal targets.  By \(\textnormal{lem:ordinary-id-formula-or-hedge}\), these two cases are exhaustive and coincide respectively with identification and nonidentification.  Thus SA-CS-ID reduces to the Shpitser--Pearl formula-or-hedge classification, while (11)--(12) prove the claimed equality of model semantics.

added_lemmas.statement: For every encoded nonterminal state \(\zeta\) produced by the initial-token compiler, if \(\zeta\) is not residual-ready, then the head of its regenerated agenda is eligible for exactly the case selected by the recursive splitter: selector correction while \(\Sigma\ne\varnothing\), and thereafter removal of nonancestors, proper-district splitting, or reachable fixing in that order.  Executing the head deletes it and leaves exactly the dependency-topologically ordered unexecuted suffix.  Consequently the machine cannot be stuck before a residual-ready state, and it never executes an ineligible preloaded token.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a compiler-produced state \(\zeta\).  If \(\Sigma\ne\varnothing\), the construction of the selector agenda lists only occurrences actually present in a labelled kernel \(K_{s,D}\), with \(s\in H\), a known zero--one gate row, and its known override value.  These are precisely the eligibility predicates in \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\).  Hence the first token is eligible, its transition deletes exactly that token, and selector rewriting creates no new gate occurrence.  Induction on \(|\Sigma|\) therefore exhausts the selector agenda.

Suppose now that \(\Sigma=\varnothing\).  The compiler tests three mutually ordered cases.  If
\[
Z=R\setminus\operatorname{an}(Y)
\]
is nonempty, it creates the unique sum token with this \(Z\); thus \(Z\subseteq R\setminus\operatorname{an}(Y)\), which is the sum-transition eligibility condition in \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\).  If \(Z=\varnothing\) and the current induced CADMG has at least two districts, the compiler creates the district token whose labels are the current kernel labels; the districts are proper, so the second eligibility test in \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\) holds.  If neither elimination case holds but a vertex \(W\) is reachable, the compiler chooses the least such vertex.  By the definition of reachability,
\[
W\in R\cap D,
\qquad
\operatorname{dis}_{D}(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_{D}(W)=\{W\},
\]
and the compiler attaches the required current labelled kernel and ledger certificate.  These are exactly the predicates of \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\).  Finally, if none of the three cases holds, residual-readiness is true by the construction of \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\).

In each nonresidual case the agenda is dependency-topologically ordered.  Its first element has no unexecuted predecessor and is therefore eligible; deletion of that element leaves precisely the unexecuted suffix, and regeneration preserves the same ordering.  The cases are exhaustive by the definition of the recursive splitter.  Thus every non-residual-ready state has the asserted eligible head, whereas a residual-ready state has no nonresidual operation to preload.

added_lemmas.statement: Let a successful finite derivation of Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser use only selector values in \(H\) and supported denominators.  Its compiled dependency-topological trace is executed by the deterministic schedule.  After \(k\) scheduled steps, every emitted labelled kernel equals, after gate reinsertion, the corresponding one among the first \(k\) published kernels; every registered denominator is the corresponding supported context normalizer or fixing margin, together with any reduced factor certified by the positivity ledger; and the regenerated agenda is exactly the unexecuted suffix of the compiled published trace.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let the published derivation DAG have \(m<\infty\) nodes.  Finiteness follows from the finite input graph and finite alphabets.  Order its nodes dependency-topologically and use the published stable vertex and context orders to break ties, as required by \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\).  We prove the assertion for \(k=0,\ldots,m\).

For \(k=0\), the context kernel for every context \(s\) used by the derivation is
\[
q_s(v)
=p_H(V=v\mid S=s)
=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{p_H(S=s)},
\qquad
p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v':(v',s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v',s).
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(s\in H\), exact selector support makes the sum in (1) nonempty, and admissible-cell interior makes every displayed summand positive.  Thus the initialized kernel and its registered normalizer are exactly the published ones.  No derivation node has been executed, so the agenda is the whole ordered trace.

Assume the invariant after \(k<m\) steps.  Dependency-topological ordering makes the head node applicable to the kernels already emitted.  If it is a selector-gate occurrence, the stored multiplexer at context \(s\) is the zero--one identity
\[
X=\mathbf 1\{I_s=0\}f_X(\operatorname{pa}_X,U_X)
  +\mathbf 1\{I_s=1\}x_s
\]
in the categorical row encoding.  Substitution at \(I_s=1\) replaces the occurrence by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\) and substitutes \(x_s\) in its children.  Recursive evaluation therefore gives the same context kernel, and gate reinsertion recovers the published occurrence.

If the head removes nonancestors \(Z\), finite distributivity gives exactly
\[
\sum_Z\prod_{j\in L}K_j.
\tag{2}
\]
If it splits a multi-district graph, the fixed normalized topological quotient gives the same ordered district factors as the published recursion.  If it fixes a reachable vertex \(W\) in district \(D\), both recursions use
\[
K'_{s,D}=\frac{K_{s,D}}{m_{s,W}},
\qquad
m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}.
\tag{3}
\]
Cross-multiplication by \(m_{s,W}\) proves equality of the predecessor and successor identities.  By the hypothesis on the published derivation, (3) is a supported margin.  Every denominator remaining after exact cancellation is registered with the factorization demanded by the ledger, and \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) makes every such factor strictly positive at \(O_H(\theta)\), for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\).

Equations (1)--(3) prove the kernel and denominator parts of the invariant at step \(k+1\).  The transition deletes exactly the head node.  The compiler's regeneration rule therefore leaves exactly nodes \(k+2,\ldots,m\), in the same dependency-topological order.  This closes the induction.

added_lemmas.statement: For a finite recursive semi-Markovian causal graph on \(V\), the Shpitser--Pearl ID recursion terminates and is sound and complete for the interventional distribution \(p\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}\): it returns a finite observed-law expression on every identified input, and otherwise returns a hedge.  The hedge proof supplies two finite binary response-function models with the same observational law and different interventional targets, using the parity construction on the returned pair of rooted confounded forests.

source.verbatim_statement: The algorithm returns either an expression derivable from P or a hedge which witnesses the non-identifiability of the effect.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the introduction on page 1220 of the AAAI paper and checked against Figure 3, Theorems 4--6, and Corollary 2 in the publisher PDF.

added_lemmas.statement: Assume \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), every selector gate is laid back on \(E_H\), and \(S\) has no latent root shared with \(V\).  At every ordinary residual, the initial-token compiler translates a successful Shpitser--Pearl ID recursion into a verifier-accepted projection circuit.  If ID returns a hedge, the compiler translates it into rational affine maps \(b\mapsto(\theta_b^+,\theta_b^-)\) on a nonempty rational open interval \(\mathcal B_H\) such that both parameters lie in \(\Theta_H\), their complete observed laws agree and have strictly positive cells and selector support exactly \(H\), and their targets differ throughout \(\mathcal B_H\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Suppress the constant selector coordinate and write \(\bar G=G_H^N\).  By the three hypotheses and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), \(\bar G\) is a finite recursive semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), its observed table is \(p_H(V,s_{\emptyset})=p(V)\), and its target is the ordinary \(p\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}\).  Invoke \(\textnormal{lem:ordinary-id-formula-or-hedge}\).

On a successful ID recursion, every line is one of marginalization over nonancestors, factorization into proper districts, or passage to a reachable subproblem by a topological quotient.  These are respectively the sum, district, and fixing cases compiled by \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\).  Induction over the finite recursion tree therefore translates the returned expression into a circuit made of additions, multiplications, substitutions, and divisions by observed margins.  Since admissible-cell positivity is full-cell positivity when \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), every such margin is positive; the ledger registers it, and cross-multiplication gives
\[
D\,t_{a,H}^N=P(o_H^N)
\quad\text{on }\mathcal I_H.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the projection candidate \(P/D\) passes the residual verifier.

Suppose instead that ID returns a hedge \((F,F')\).  The cited hedge construction gives two binary canonical models \(M^+_0,M^-_0\) whose observed laws on \(F\) are equal and uniform on the even-parity class, while some component of their post-intervention root distribution, and hence of the target after the standard descendant extension, differs.  Choose a root vertex \(R_0\) of the confounded forest; it has no child inside \(F\).  In both models augment the response table of \(R_0\) by the same independent Bernoulli flip \(B_\delta\), with rational \(0<\delta<1/2\).  If \(p_0\) and \(p_1\) denote the uniform laws on the even and odd parity classes, respectively, then both observational laws on \(F\) become
\[
p_\delta=(1-\delta)p_0+\delta p_1
          =(1-2\delta)p_0+2\delta u_F,
\qquad
u_F=\frac{p_0+p_1}{2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Here \(u_F\) is the strictly positive uniform law on all binary cells.  Hence every cell of \(p_\delta\) is positive.  Equality of the two observed laws is preserved because exactly the same Markov kernel, the flip of the childless coordinate \(R_0\), is applied to their common observed law.

Set every vertex outside \(F\) that is not needed for target transmission to a common rational full-support kernel using its dedicated response error; permitted extra graphical arguments may be ignored.  Along the directed extension from the hedge roots to \(Y\), use common rational full-support binary channels arbitrarily close to the injective deterministic channels in the classical construction.  Conditional on the already equal law on \(F\), these common kernels preserve equality of the complete observed law.  Because the kernel at every added vertex has strictly positive entries, (5) and recursive factorization imply, one vertex at a time, that every full observed cell is strictly positive.

Let \(\Delta(\delta,\varepsilon)\) be a target-table component difference, where \(\varepsilon\) collects the crossover probabilities of the added channels.  Finite recursive evaluation makes \(\Delta\) a polynomial with rational coefficients.  At \((\delta,\varepsilon)=(0,0)\), the classical hedge construction gives \(\Delta(0,0)\ne0\).  Continuity therefore supplies an open neighborhood on which \(\Delta\) has constant nonzero sign.  Rational points are dense, so choose rational positive \((\delta_0,\varepsilon_0)\) in that neighborhood with \(\delta_0<1/2\).  All observed cells at that point are positive.  A second continuity argument and finiteness of the cell set give rational numbers \(0<\ell<\delta_0<u<1/2\) such that, with \(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0\) fixed, every observed cell stays positive and \(\Delta(\delta,\varepsilon_0)\ne0\) for \(\ell<\delta<u\).

Take \(b=\delta\) and \(\mathcal B_H=(\ell,u)\).  The response probability of the flip row is affine in \(b\), and all other primitive probabilities are fixed rational numbers; hence \(b\mapsto(\theta_b^+,\theta_b^-)\) is rational affine.  The canonical-response-richness assumption realizes each rational full-support kernel as a probability law on finite response functions.  The selector equation is the same deterministic constant in both models, so its support is exactly \(H\).  We have proved for all \(b\in\mathcal B_H\)
\[
\theta_b^+,\theta_b^-\in\Theta_H,
\qquad
O_H(\theta_b^+)=O_H(\theta_b^-),
\qquad
T_{a,H}(\theta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^-).
\tag{6}
\]
All identities in (4)--(6) are finite polynomial identities or strict rational inequalities, so the corresponding projection or contrast candidate passes \(\textnormal{def:residual-transition}\).

proposed.name: support-aware initial and regenerated token compiler
proposed.construction: Given the normalized retained expansion \(G_H^N\), form the initial selector agenda by listing exactly the selector-gate occurrences that are present in context-labelled kernels with labels \(s\in H\), in the topological order of \(G_H^N\) and then the lexicographic context and row order.  Every listed selector token is support licensed and syntactically eligible.  After the selector agenda is empty, apply the following recursive case splitter to the current labelled CADMG problem: first remove the nonempty set of nonancestors of \(Y\), if any; otherwise split when the current graph has more than one district; otherwise apply the canonically least reachable fixing operation, if one exists; and declare the state residual-ready exactly when none of these three cases applies.  At initialization and after every transition, retain only the dependency-topologically ordered agenda for the chosen current case; no token preceding the first eligible token is stored.  For a successful derivation produced by Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser using contexts in \(H\), compile its finite derivation DAG in dependency-topological order, breaking ties by the published stable vertex order and then context order.  The remaining agenda is regenerated as exactly the unexecuted suffix after deletion of the executed head.  The compiler introduces no transition relation other than \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\), and \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The four transition relations need an explicit recursive agenda compiler to guarantee nonresidual progress and faithful scheduling of published traces.

proposed.name: support-aware completeness handle
proposed.construction: Starting from the normalized primitive carrier and retained constraints, apply the initial-token compiler and expose exactly four finite transition relations: support-licensed selector correction, reachable fixing, labelled rational elimination, and residual certificate compilation.  The compiler regenerates the agenda by the standard recursive ID case splitter and declares a state residual-ready only when removal of nonancestors, proper-district splitting, and reachable fixing are all inapplicable.  Carry polynomial identities and branch denominators with each state; at an irreducible residual search the finite projection and signed-row-swap libraries for either an observable rational circuit or one common response-table contrast that preserves all contexts in \(H\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The handle must expose the directive-required agenda compiler and its residual-readiness test.

proposed.name: executable SA-CS-ID transition system
proposed.construction: Encode the initial tuple \(\zeta_0\) by \(\operatorname{enc}_H\), with agendas produced by the initial-token compiler.  Repeatedly apply the first eligible relation among \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\), and \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\) under \(\mathfrak P_H\).  After an admitted transition, regenerate the agenda as the dependency-topologically ordered unexecuted suffix prescribed by the compiler; in particular, an ineligible token is never placed before the next eligible token.  A transition is admitted only after its finite syntactic eligibility test and exact polynomial local obligation succeed, and the successor must have smaller \(\mu_H\).  The residual relation is the only halting relation and emits either the verified rational circuit with its denominator domain or the verified global-twin box.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Machine execution must initialize and regenerate only the dependency-ordered agenda selected by the standard recursive case splitter.

proposed.statement: Each eligible selector-correction, reachable-fixing, labelled-elimination, and residual-compilation transition preserves the represented observation-target relation on its registered branch domain after composing its emitted circuit, and discharges exactly its displayed polynomial identity or inequality obligation. For every nonhalting transition \(\zeta\Rightarrow\zeta'\), \(\mu_H(\zeta')<_{\mathrm{lex}}\mu_H(\zeta)\): selector correction removes one \(\sigma\)-token, fixing removes one active vertex, elimination removes a nonempty active set or one \(\ell\)-token, and residual compilation removes the sole residual token and enters a terminal state. Therefore the deterministic schedule terminates after finitely many encoded transitions, conditional only on the residual verifier finding a candidate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The established transition theorem must consume the new nonresidual-progress invariant supplied by the explicit agenda compiler.

proposed.statement: Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\) such that \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\) and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). Gate reinsertion makes the returned circuit and its required positive margins algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The preservation proof now directly uses the compiled published-trace invariant and nonresidual progress.

proposed.statement: If \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), every selector gate is laid back on \(E_H\), and \(S\) has no latent root shared with \(V\), then \(G_H^N\) is the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), \(\Phi_H\) equals its ordinary observational-target relation, and \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) reduces to the ID formula-or-hedge classification of Shpitser and Pearl.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The ordinary reduction is proved independently of the open general residual dichotomy by the dedicated ordinary residual compiler.

proposed.statement: For every input \((G^{+},H,A,a,Y)\) satisfying the model assumptions, the machine whose schedule contains only \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\) terminates and returns exactly one sound certificate. On each transition the stated local polynomial obligation holds and \(\mu_H\) decreases lexicographically. It returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\), with \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\), if and only if \(T_{a,H}(\theta_1)=T_{a,H}(\theta_2)\) for all \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta_H\) satisfying \(O_H(\theta_1)=O_H(\theta_2)\); otherwise it returns a support-exact global-twin box. Thus \(F_H\) is partial on the ambient simplex but covers the complete compatible fixed-support image on an identified branch. This strictly completes Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser for the declared fixed-support class without adding a selector context.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline remains unchanged and open, but its declared spine must include the explicit nonresidual compiler and progress theorem while retaining the general residual OEQ.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The general residual converse: every irreducible fixed-support residual must contain either a verifier-accepted rational projection identity or one verifier-accepted common signed response-row contrast.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen primitives do not prove that target constancy on fibers of the polynomial observation map implies a rational circuit in the finite projection library; a fiber-constant target can in principle descend only as a nonrational algebraic function. On the negative side, the ordinary hedge perturbation and the terminal tensor contrast need not lift through several interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants without changing at least one supported observed cell. This is exactly the sibling open question on which the unchanged headline depends.
open_obligations.attempted: The Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser recursive district and fixing construction was compiled on the projection side, and the Kivva--Mokhtarian--Etesami--Kiyavash positivity strategy was pursued on the witness side. Rational interior mixing closes the ordinary hedge case and the presolve closes the terminal three-observable case. For a general residual, however, the common contrast must lie simultaneously in the kernels of all context observation maps while retaining nonzero target derivative; neither districtwise contrasts nor generic elimination prove that common-kernel alternative or exclude a nonrational identified quotient.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The normalization equivalence, local transition soundness, denominator positivity, and lexicographic decrease are established.  The initial-token compiler and nonresidual-progress lemma now show that the deterministic machine cannot stop before a residual-ready state, and the published-trace lemma proves preservation of every successful Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser derivation using only \(H\).  Certificate soundness proves
\[
F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
\Longrightarrow
T_{a,H}\text{ is constant on every }O_H\text{-fiber},
\]
whereas any returned twin box exhibits a nonconstant fiber.  The ordinary no-selection residual is completely compiled to a Shpitser--Pearl formula or a strictly positive rational hedge-twin box.  What remains is the converse at a general fixed-support residual: proving that fiber constancy forces one of the finite rational projection identities, and that failure of fiber constancy forces one common signed response-row contrast that survives all interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants while preserving exactly \(H\).

prose_updates.tldr: For a finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCM observed on exactly \(H\), the intrinsic normalized carrier and its retained constraints are equivalent to the original fixed-support parameterization. The executable four-transition machine now has an explicit recursive agenda compiler: it cannot stop before a residual-ready state, it faithfully schedules every successful Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser trace that uses only supplied contexts, and it reduces to the complete Shpitser--Pearl formula-or-hedge classification when selection disappears. Returned formulas and returned twin boxes are sound. The field-level all-residual converse remains open: no proof yet excludes an identified fixed-support residual with only a nonrational algebraic functional or guarantees a common support-preserving contrast through arbitrary interacting districts.

project_justification.fill: The project constructs the intrinsic normalized carrier \(\Lambda_H\), proves its constrained subset \(\mathcal I_H\) equals the original fixed-support image, and develops an exact four-relation SA-CS-ID machine with local algebraic obligations, a complete positivity ledger, and an explicit recursive agenda compiler. The proved positive layer preserves supported Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser derivations, and the no-selection specialization has a rational formula-or-strictly-positive-hedge-twin compiler. The intended field-level completion is still conditional on proving the general all-residual rational-projection-or-common-contrast dichotomy.

prose_updates.interpretation: Support-active normalization and scheduling solve the representation and nonresidual progress problems without introducing an unsupplied selector context. They do not by themselves turn fiberwise causal identification into a rational observed-law circuit. The ordinary hedge lift shows how a common rational positive mixture yields legal global twins in the no-selection endpoint; extending that construction through coupled fixed-support districts is the remaining mathematical kernel.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The terminal response contrast, the ordinary positive hedge lift, and the explicit worked twins do not prove that the finite residual candidate library succeeds on every interacting-district state. A residual may require a nonrational algebraic functional, or every available signed row-swap contrast may alter an observed descendant or a fixed context kernel. Either event defeats the rational formula-or-global-twin headline and requires a pivot. Boundary-uniform inference, off-domain regularization, and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established are normalization equivalence; local transition soundness and lexicographic decrease; positivity of every admitted denominator; nonresidual agenda progress; preservation of successful published traces using only \(H\); soundness of every returned certificate; and the complete ordinary-ID reduction with a strictly positive rational hedge-twin lift. Still to prove is success of the residual verifier on every general fixed-support irreducible state, including exclusion of identified nonrational residuals and construction of a single common contrast through interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants. The headline completeness theorem remains open through exactly that obligation. Pointwise interior Wald inference is separate; no boundary-uniform guarantee or common numerical positivity bound is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit trace compiler proves that every successful supported anchor derivation is actually selected by the deterministic machine and retains the same kernels and positive margins after gate reinsertion.
statement_notes.gap: Prior formula-transport results do not provide this fixed-support retained-image scheduling invariant.
statement_notes.consumer: Existing systematic-selection analyses can use the normalized positive backend without changing a valid formula or silently adding a context.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the field-level target: it would upgrade the proved normalization, scheduling, and certificate semantics to a complete fixed-support causal identification calculus.
statement_notes.gap: The exact unresolved gap is the all-residual rational-projection-or-common-contrast converse, including exclusion of an identified residual whose functional is algebraic but nonrational.
statement_notes.consumer: A complete dosearch backend with exhaustive model-level semantics must wait for this residual theorem; the proved positive and ordinary-ID layers can already be regression-tested.

statement_notes.justification: The proved reduction shows that the support-aware compiler agrees with classical completeness when systematic selection disappears.
statement_notes.gap: The dedicated ordinary residual compiler removes any dependence of this sanity check on the still-open general selector residual theorem.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementers can regression-test formula outputs and strictly positive hedge-twin certificates against established ordinary ID cases.
